output.summary: The board is declaring certain district vehicles obsolete and surplus under Resolution No. 2021-0087. This lets the district get rid of them. The item lists no dollar amounts.

output.summary: The board is declaring certain district equipment obsolete and surplus under Resolution No. 2021-0088. This lets the district get rid of them. The item lists no dollar amounts.

output.summary: The board is declaring certain district equipment obsolete and surplus under Resolution No. 2021-0121. This lets the district get rid of them. The item lists no dollar amounts.

output.headline: Moves $16,000 of Madison Park's Measure N money from transportation to teacher training pay
output.summary: The board is approving a Measure N Commission recommendation to move $16,000 at Madison Park Academy from transportation costs, which are not needed during distance learning, to extended teacher contracts for teacher training and assignment mastery. The change applies to 2020-2021. It moves existing Measure N money and the text says it has no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Extends East Bay Asian Youth Center's Roosevelt Middle School learning pod at no added cost
output.summary: This changes a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with East Bay Asian Youth Center, which provides in-person learning supports to grade 6-8 students at Roosevelt Middle School, through an updated scope of work. There is no added cost, and the limit stays at $399,538 for August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021. The agreement period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Pays Star Elevator $39,435 to modify the Fremont High passenger elevator's fire circuitry, without bidding
output.summary: Star Elevator of San Carlos will provide labor and materials to modify the fire service circuitry on the passenger elevator for the Fremont High School New Construction Project. The $39,435.00 includes a $2,030.33 contingency, and the Board is approving this agreement without competitive bidding. Work is scheduled from February 11 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Moves $13,700 of Castlemont's Measure N money from transportation to teacher project leads
output.summary: The board is approving a Measure N Commission recommendation to move a total of $13,700 at Castlemont High School from four transportation items, which are not needed during distance learning, to extended teacher contracts for teachers who will lead the CastleWorks projects. The change applies to 2020-2021. It moves existing Measure N money and the text says it has no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Moves $50,000 of Coliseum College Prep's Measure N money to pay for a case manager position
output.summary: The board is approving a Measure N Commission recommendation to move a total of $50,000 at Coliseum College Preparatory Academy, $8,000 from supplies and materials and $42,000 from teacher salary stipends, to clerical salaries to open a case manager position. The text says less is needed for extended contracts during distance learning. The change applies to 2020-2021. It moves existing Measure N money and the text says it has no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Moves $3,125 of Skyline's Measure N money from substitutes to teacher collaboration pay
output.summary: The board is approving a Measure N Commission recommendation to move $3,125 at Skyline High School from teacher substitutes to stipends for extended teacher contracts for collaboration and professional development time. The change applies to 2020-2021. It moves existing Measure N money and the text says it has no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Moves $7,000 of Skyline's Measure N money from conferences to teacher collaboration pay
output.summary: The board is approving a Measure N Commission recommendation to move $7,000 at Skyline High School from conference expenses, which the text says are unlikely to be used, to stipends for extended teacher contracts for collaboration and professional development time. The change applies to 2020-2021. It moves existing Measure N money and the text says it has no fiscal impact.

output.headline: Moves $5,000 at Skyline High from unused transportation costs to arts technology equipment

money.evidence: transferring $5,000.00 from strategic action Transportation costs

output.summary: The Board is asked to approve a request from Skyline High School to move $5,000 within its 2020-21 Measure N budget. The money comes from transportation costs, which the school says have little impact because field trips will likely not be possible, and goes to equipment for visual and performing arts technology. This shifts existing funds and does not add new money.

output.headline: Moves $1,500 at Skyline High from conference expenses to arts technology equipment

The money comes from conference expenses, which the school says have little impact because travel to conferences will likely not be possible, and goes to equipment for visual and performing arts technology. This shifts existing funds and does not add new money.

output.headline: Ends Year 3 of the district's contract with School Innovations & Achievement, effective July 1, 2021
output.summary: The board is ending Year 3 of the district's good governance and program advisory services contract with School Innovations & Achievement, effective July 1, 2021. The termination is "for convenience," meaning the district is ending it without a claim that the company failed to perform. The item lists no dollar amounts.

output.headline: Accepts a free online web development class from ScriptEd (Code Nation) for students
output.summary: ScriptEd, which does business as Code Nation, will teach its Intro to Web Development curriculum online to district students twice a week for 45 to 60 minutes, live, from January 1, 2021 through June 30, 2021. It costs the district nothing.

output.headline: Accepts free career mentoring for high school students from OverCOME
output.summary: OverCOME will match high school students from underserved or academically disadvantaged backgrounds with mentors in fields that interest them, set personal goals, and help connect them to job shadowing and internships. The agreement runs from December 15, 2020 through November 19, 2021 and costs the district nothing.

output.headline: Extends Oakland Kids First's Castlemont High learning pod at no added cost
output.summary: This changes a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Oakland Kids First, which gives grade 9-12 students at Castlemont High School in-person help with technology, online class access, motivation and mentoring. There is no added cost, and the limit stays at $197,238 for July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021. The agreement period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Asian Youth Center up to $91,000 for attendance support at Garfield Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $91,000.00

output.summary: East Bay Asian Youth Center will work with Garfield Elementary staff to find students at risk of chronic absence, case-manage those students and families, and run monthly attendance raffles and virtual assemblies. The cost is up to $91,000 for September 1, 2020 through May 28, 2021. The agreement period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for Reading Partners tutoring at Laurel Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with Reading Partners to run a reading tutoring program for identified students at Laurel Elementary School. The cost is up to $10,000 for August 10, 2020 through May 28, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $2,900 to Servio Consulting's contract to update the COVID daily assessment survey
output.summary: The district is paying Servio Consulting $2,900 more to reprogram its COVID Daily Assessment survey so later questions can depend on earlier answers, across web, text and voice. This raises the contract limit from $35,000 to $37,900 for September 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021. The contract period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Pays Girls Inc. of Alameda County up to $14,093 to tutor Bridges Academy students in reading

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $14,093.00

output.summary: Girls Inc. will give small-group, 30-minute tutoring sessions two to four times a week to at least 40 students at Bridges Academy @ Melrose who read between one month and two and a half years below grade level. The cost is up to $14,093 for August 19, 2020 through May 27, 2021. The agreement period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Pays Girls Inc. of Alameda County up to $907 for tutoring at Bridges Academy in August 2020

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $907.00

output.summary: Girls Inc. gave small-group, 30-minute reading tutoring sessions to students at Bridges Academy @ Melrose who read below grade level, for the short period of August 10, 2020 through August 19, 2020. The cost is up to $907. This period ended well before the board vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $18,250 for an enriched science program at Sequoia Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $18,250.00

output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement with an individual contractor to teach an enriched science program for 30 minutes a week to all TK-5th grade students at Sequoia Elementary School. The cost is up to $18,250 for February 1, 2021 through May 14, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,500 for Luna Dance Institute's dance program at Grass Valley Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $12,500.00

output.summary: The board is approving after the fact an agreement for Luna Dance Institute to continue building a dance program at Grass Valley Elementary School for students with and without disabilities. The cost is up to $12,500 for September 1, 2020 through May 14, 2021.

output.headline: Allows student data to be shared with UCSF for a school re-opening safety study
output.summary: The district will send student data to the University of California, San Francisco for a study of indoor school settings in the Bay Area, looking at how well CDC guidelines for safely re-opening schools work. The agreement covers how the data is sent and protected, and runs from January 12, 2021 through June 11, 2021. The text states no cost.

The cost is up to $45,000 for August 10, 2020 through May 28, 2021. The agreement period began before the board vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $19,500 for Higher Gliffs to lead a Fremont High mural project

The cost is up to $19,500 for January 4, 2021 through May 27, 2021.

output.headline: Allows student data to be shared with the University of Delaware for a free curriculum study
output.summary: The district will share data with the University of Delaware, which will run a no-cost research study on how best to support high-quality curricula in the district. The agreement runs from January 8, 2021 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Extends WestEd's science standards grant to March 2021 with the amount unchanged at $501,930
output.summary: This changes a grant award and subcontract with WestEd that supports the California Next Generation Science Standards K-8 Early Implementation Initiative, covering Years 5 and 6. It only extends the term, through March 31, 2021, and the amount stays at $501,930. The wording of the old and new dates in the text is unclear.

output.headline: Carries over $1.83M in unspent 2019-20 Measure N funds for named district and charter schools
output.summary: This resolution lets named district and charter schools carry over their unspent 2019-20 Measure N funds, which support college and career readiness, into the next budget. The cumulative amount is $1,831,416.23. The text does not list the individual schools.

output.headline: Awards Common Vision up to $864,000 to deliver district meals and produce boxes to homes

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $864,000.00

output.summary: Common Vision of Berkeley won a competitive bid to deliver meals the district prepares, along with produce boxes, to students' homes. The contract is for up to $864,000 from February 15, 2021 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Carries over $20,123.97 in unspent 2019-20 Measure G1 funds for named district middle schools
output.summary: This resolution lets named district middle schools carry over unspent 2019-20 Measure G1 funds, which pay for teacher retention and middle school improvement, and approves their plans for using the money. The cumulative amount is $20,123.97. The text does not list the individual schools.
